brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Single full hex base with solid top cover as clock face; rear accessory hex-acc-keyhole provides keyhole wall hanger; caps and lockJoints applied

Configurator checks fit only and has no clock movement, motor or bearing parts; prints are static plastic. Two pencil props placed on cover serve as static hour/minute hands approximating ~3 o'clock, but do not rotate or keep time. No material/process can provide movement.
Decorative face with two hands points to a readable time position when viewed from above, but is not a functioning timekeeper; no mechanism to track or update time.

finish.summary: Built modest wall clock mockup: full hex base with top cover as dial, keyhole hanger on back for wall mounting, two pencil props as static hands. Movement cannot be provided - Hex Cluster is static 3D-printed construction with no clockwork/movement parts, and configurator only verifies fit/collisions, not function. Hands are decorative only.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
